questions.question: Which OSI layer routes IP packets between networks?
questions.explanation: The Network layer (Layer 3) moves packets between networks using logical addresses.

option_explanations.A: Physical carries signals that represent bits.
option_explanations.B: Data Link delivers frames over a local link using link-layer addresses.
option_explanations.C: The Network layer (Layer 3) moves packets between networks using logical addresses.
option_explanations.D: Transport serves end-to-end conversations, for example using TCP or UDP ports.

questions.question: Which two fields in an Ethernet frame identify the sending and receiving interfaces?
questions.explanation: Ethernet carries source and destination MAC addresses. IP addresses and UDP ports are fields in higher-layer protocol headers.

option_explanations.A: The source MAC identifies the frame's sender on the local link.
option_explanations.B: The destination IPv4 address belongs to an IP packet, not the Ethernet header.
option_explanations.C: The destination MAC identifies the intended receiver or group on the Ethernet link.
option_explanations.D: The UDP source port belongs to the transport header rather than the Ethernet header.

questions.question: Which transport protocol provides a reliable ordered byte stream?
questions.explanation: TCP uses sequence numbers and acknowledgements to deliver an ordered byte stream. UDP does not provide these guarantees.

option_explanations.A: IP carries packets without guaranteeing ordered delivery.
option_explanations.B: UDP carries datagrams without ordered, reliable byte-stream semantics.
option_explanations.C: ICMP reports network conditions and supports diagnostics rather than application streams.
option_explanations.D: TCP uses sequence numbers and acknowledgements to deliver an ordered byte stream. UDP does not provide these guarantees.
